Decision history
Architecture, not test syntax

Four layers. One stable intent.

Farley’s separation keeps business examples independent of the mechanisms used to exercise a system. “Intent” is our review policy, separate from a file’s architectural layer.

Would it survive a rewrite?

A useful intent test describes a rule that should remain true even if you replace the implementation.

Gherkin can express intent
“A court cannot be booked twice for the same time.”
Unit tests can express intent too
“Adjacent bookings do not overlap.” A pure domain rule need not be expressed in Gherkin to deserve protection.
The plumbing can change meaning too.
A step definition, fixture, driver, or test configuration can weaken a specification. Classify important supporting artifacts as intent too, and review indirect changes in your repository.

The working loop

  1. Agree one small example with a human.
  2. Accept and protect the executable test.
  3. Observe it fail against the real system.
  4. Let AI change the implementation to pass.
  5. Run the contract. Review any proposed intent change.

Inspired by Dave Farley’s ATDD guide ↗. The classification and review workflow here are our design, not an official Farley product. The exact recent article has not been identified.

Take the contract into your repository.

Download a baseline, a change detector, and the instructions for your coding agent.

Prototype boundary: this browser stores data locally. Reviewer names are self-declared, not authenticated. Approvals here are a workflow demonstration; they do not approve Git changes or run tests. Repository enforcement requires a trusted CI check and protected human review.
01 / BASELINE

intent-policy.json

SHA-256 fingerprints of accepted intent files, plus classifications and reasons. Pending proposals never enter the baseline.

02 / VERIFICATION

check_intent.py

A dependency-free check that detects modified or missing protected files. Run it against the policy from your trusted base branch.

03 / AGENT CONTRACT

AI-INSTRUCTIONS.md

A bootstrap prompt with the accepted contract, boundaries, and a safe small-step workflow for your coding agent.

Make human review a real gate

Keep the policy and checker under human ownership. Configure branch protection to require a trusted check and code-owner approval for protected files, policy changes, the checker, and CI configuration. Dismiss stale approvals when commits change. Do not grant the coding agent approval or bypass privileges.

# Export the BASE branch policy to a trusted path first.
# Run the checker from the base branch / trusted CI configuration.
python3 check_intent.py --policy /trusted/base/intent-policy.json --root .

The check intentionally fails on every protected file change, including deletion or rename. A reviewer must explicitly approve a baseline update in the repository. Local decisions are not imported as proof of approval. File hashes cannot detect all changes in test discovery, dependencies, or runtime behaviour; run the tests separately.

Source import creates one artifact per file. Mixed files are protected in full; split files when only selected tests should be protected. Imports are text only and never executed.
